name: When should I repair my roof versus replacing it?

mainEntity.name: When should I repair my roof versus replacing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deciding between repair and replacement depends on the age of your roof, the extent of the damage, and the overall condition. If your roof is relatively new (under 15-20 years old) and the damage is localized (e.g., a few missing shingles or a small leak), a repair is often the more cost-effective solution. However, if your roof is nearing the end of its lifespan, has widespread damage, or multiple leaks, a full replacement might be a better long-term investment to prevent recurring issues.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repair when damage is localized and the roof is relatively new. Consider replacement if the roof is old, has widespread damage, or multiple recurring issues.
